newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan deports N.Korean captain of drug-laden boat.
newsitem.headline: Japan deports N.Korean captain of drug-laden boat.

text.p: Japanese authorities deported the captain of a North Korean freighter that was seized with a large cache of illegal drugs last month, officials said on Thursday.

Captain Maeng Song-chul, a 50-year-old North Korean national arrested on April 10, was put aboard a Cambodian freighter bound for North Korea on Wednesday, immigration officials in the southern city of Fukuoka said.

Maeng and two other North Korean crewmen, who have already returned to North Korea, were arrested on suspicion of smuggling stimulants in cargo labelled as honey on the North Korean-registered freighter Ji Song-2.

The 1,499-tonne Ji Song-2, which left the North Korean port of Nanpo on April 5 for the Japanese port, was searched at Hososhima island on the Pacific coast of Kyushu island and 70 kg (154 lb) of amphetamines, with a street value estimated at $95 million were found, police said.
Two Koreans from an Osaka-based trading firm arrested after the seizure were indicted for drug law violations on May 9 for their suspected role in the smuggling attempt.
Japanese analysts said the drug smuggling could be a sign that North Korea, impoverished and facing near-famine conditions has turned to new means to raise cash from Japan.
Donations to Pyongyang by residents of Japan of North Korean descent, a legacy of Tokyo's 1910-45 colonisation of Korea, are a key source of hard currency for the isolated Stalinist government.
The boat seizure was cited by Japan as a reason why it is reluctant to join the United States, South Korea and other states in responding to international appeals to help North Korea.
Japan's public opinion is torn between humanitarian concern for starving North Koreans and antipathy toward Pyongyang, which many suspect has kidnapped Japanese citizens over the past two decades.
Japan's already chilly ties with North Korea worsened recently after a North Korean defector said northern agents kidnapped a Japanese schoolgirl who had disappeared in 1977.
